conventions: The two Sh tokens of this chapter — the paragogic he of הַקְשִׁיבָה (142.6) and of הוֹצִיאָה (142.7) — are each their own `unrepresented` unit under rule 32, and MACULA's glosses on them (*attention*, *out*) are the host word's gloss distributed across its segments in reverse order, the display defect rule 39 describes. The second is the trap: *out* stands in 142.7's target, but it is the English phrasal particle of הוֹצִיא → *Bring ... out* and belongs to the verb under rule 44, the ablative מִן taking the *of* beside it. Read the morphology tag and not the gloss; the he takes nothing in either verse.
report: All 9 candidate lemmas checked; none is a split. The closest are the 1cs-suffixed prepositions: לְ is *for* at 142.3 (טָמְנוּ פַח לִי → *hidden a snare for me*, its own relation written) and unrepresented at 142.4 (אֵין־לִי מַכִּיר → *no man that knoweth me*, its object promoted to the English verb's object, rule 40); מִן is unrepresented at 142.4 (*hath failed me*) and *than* at 142.6 (comparative, rule 24, 119 bare corpus units). Each difference is licensed by what the ASV writes, not by a change of analysis.

עַל → *within* (142.3) and *with* (142.7) is one preposition in two clauses, against a corpus carrying hundreds of renderings of it. The two אַיִן of 142.4 differ only in that the ASV writes the presentative frame for the first and not the second; rule 50 aligns what is written, and both shapes are heavily attested (69 units *there is no*, 60 bare *no*). זָעַק differs by tense, יהוה by vocative position, and וְ by the connective written beside each waw — *and* and *For* in 142.4, none in 142.3, where the apodosis opens bare and rule 14's closing count leaves the waw unrepresented.

Read the dump end to end for the split the lemma table cannot see: supplied English marked `added` in one verse and folded into its licensing morpheme in another. The chapter has exactly one `added` unit, the italic *my* of יָמִין → *my right hand* (142.4), and it is the one place where no morpheme in the phrase licenses the supplied word. Every other supplied word is folded into the morpheme that licenses it — *with*/*With* on each קוֹל (142.1, rule 33), *the* on אֹרַח (142.3) and on צַדִּיקִים (142.7), *a* on תְּפִלָּה (142.0) and פַּח (142.3), *man that*/*man* on the two anarthrous participles (142.4, rule 46), *O* on the vocative יהוה (142.5), and the presentative frame on the first אַיִן. Consistent.

The three prepositions an English recasting silences — לִי and מִמֶּנִּי at 142.4, בִּי at 142.7 — are treated identically: preposition `unrepresented`, suffix taking the written *me*, rule 40 with rule 18. The two Sh tokens (142.6, 142.7) are treated identically as paragogic he under rule 32, notwithstanding that MACULA's reversed segment gloss offers *out* for the second and the ASV's target actually contains that word.

BSB: all six disagreements are documented convention differences and none is an error. Three (לִי, מִמֶּנִּי at 142.4; בִּי at 142.7) are rule 40/21 recastings, where BSB attaches the preposition to its phrase; two are the paragogic he of 142.6 and 142.7, which rule 32 names as the bulk of the BSB disagreements in the Psalms; one is the bare apodosis waw of 142.3, for which the ASV writes no connective. Nothing here would justify moving an accepted edge.

One convention recorded, on the Sh gloss artifact. No promotion: rule 39 already rules that a gloss contradicting surface, lemma and morphology is a display defect, and rule 32 already disposes of the paragogic he, so a contract edit here would only restate them.
